column1: # What a backstop (a clock's, or the RSS reading's) stopped in the run that set each floor in floors.tsv. A crate's rows start with <crate>
column4: <n>: that run's stops were kept, and the lane cancelled n of its proof checks. Each obligation a backstop stopped in it follows: <crate>
column7: <obligation>. `ship trust run --update-ratchet` writes a crate's rows with its floor. The judge credits a starved run's shortfall only with the stops its floor's run did not have and the cancelled proof checks beyond that run's count, so what every run has is the code's. A crate with no rows was floored before they were kept: what its floor's run stopped is unknown, so every stop and cancelled check is credited.
